scene: A cartoon man with a round cream face, navy baseball cap, black collared shirt, furrowed brows, black dot eyes and a flat mouth looks to his left at a hand holding four torn-edged hundred-dollar bills fanned out. The bills glow blue, yellow, red and green, and dashed leader lines tie the labels 50%, 20% and 15% to the first three while a second 15% sits beside the green bill next to his cheek. The room behind is a blurred dark orange-brown interior.
mechanism: Four colour-coded bills with percentage tags turn the title's 'manage your money' into a visible split, so the viewer sees a numeric formula before opening the video.
composition: The face and cap fill the right half, with the hand and bill fan on the left-centre acting as the second anchor; the labels step down along a diagonal from upper left to the green bill. The upper left and lower right are dark negative space, and the bills sit close to the face so the two read as one cluster.
typography: Four short percentage labels in thin white sans, each smaller than the bills they annotate and set without a heavy outline. At 160x90 the 50% and 20% tags are faint specks and the two 15% tags are barely distinguishable from the glow, and the labels carry no words from the title.
colors: Burnt orange and near-black background with a cream face, then four saturated glowing bills in blue, yellow, red and green as the only multi-hue accents. The glow lifts the bills off the dark ground, and the red bill is simply one of the four note colours.
psychology: Lowered, slightly angled brows and a straight closed mouth give the man a stern, assessing look while his eyes point toward the money. The fanned bills and glowing edges add a reward cue; no fear or urgency cue is visible.
partnership: The title promises a 1% money method; the thumbnail adds a four-part split of 50, 20, 15 and 15 (these sum to 100) without naming any category. The unlabelled percentages leave the question of what each slice is, which the title does not answer.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the glowing blue-to-green bill fan first, then the stern face and cap, then the 50% tag at upper left, with the second 15% last.
art: Flat-shaded cartoon with thick outlines and a soft blurred background; the bills are detailed photo-like banknotes with glow edges, so character and money use two different rendering styles. The torn edges and glow survive on a phone as colour blocks, but the serial text on the notes does not.
strength: Four differently coloured bills with percentages show a concrete split that a title alone could not.
weakness: The percentage labels are small, thin and low in contrast against the bill glow, so the numbers are the weakest-reading element.
bottleneck: The numbers carry the proposition but shrink to specks at 160x90, leaving only the stern face and coloured bills to read.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the four percentages to roughly twice their height with a dark outline to test whether the split reads at phone size.
counterexample: Seq 2 uses two words of huge yellow text that stay legible at 160x90, where this frame's numbers do not.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A stick figure with a large round white head, raised brows, eyes rolled up to the right and a flat mouth lies propped on its elbow on a straw-textured cave floor. A small campfire burns behind it, and at the right the cave mouth opens onto a dark blue night sky with a white crescent moon. The cave walls are brown with sketchy crack lines.
mechanism: A pointed numeric question over a wakeful cave sleeper sets up a surprising claim about sleep at night, and the title's open 'what did they do' gets one odd number as an answer.
composition: The headline fills the entire top band while the stick figure's head sits lower left and the moon-lit cave mouth lower right, so the eye runs left to right along the bottom. The fire in the middle ties the two halves; the figure occupies about a third of the frame and the lower half is otherwise empty brown floor.
typography: Two words with a numeral, '2 SLEEPS?', in very thick yellow capitals with a black outline spanning almost the full width, the largest element in the frame. Both words are fully readable at 160x90, and the numeral adds a claim the title does not state.
colors: Muted brown cave and black outlines set off by a yellow headline, an orange fire and a navy night patch with a white moon. The yellow is the only bright large shape, so it dominates, and the figure's white head separates cleanly from the brown ground.
psychology: Upturned brows with eyes glancing up and a flat mouth read as puzzled or wary, as if the figure is awake while the fire burns. The dark cave mouth and moon supply a night cue; no fear or alarm element appears.
partnership: The title asks what ancient humans did at night; the thumbnail answers with a number and a question mark, hinting at two separate sleeps. It leaves open why and when, so the title and image cooperate without repeating each other.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow 2 SLEEPS? headline first, then the wide-eyed stick head, then the fire and the moon in the cave mouth.
art: Flat sketchy cartoon with a simple stick-figure body, tonal cave texture and a clean blue patch for the sky. The proportions are consistent and the scene stays simple enough that headline, head and fire all read at phone size.
strength: A two-word numeric headline fills the width and answers the title with an unexpected number.
weakness: The sketchy brown cave walls and floor are low in contrast and give the lower half little to look at beyond the head.
bottleneck: The figure's lying pose is thin lines on brown, so the sleeping idea is carried by the text rather than the picture.
action: Hypothesis: add a second, lighter pose of the same figure sitting by the fire to test whether showing two sleep states makes the number self-explanatory.
counterexample: Seq 7 packs six annotation labels around its subject, where this frame holds one claim and one subject.
expression_label: raised brows, eyes up, flat mouth
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: At the left a cartoon figure with spiky black hair, a red hooded jacket, clenched bared teeth, wide eyes and blue sweat drops crouches behind a grey boulder among green bushes. At the right a long-haired figure with a white face, bulging eyes, a sharp-toothed grin with a drool drop, a red tie and a stick body holds a black rifle in a green field. A thick red curved arrow runs from below the headline to the boulder, and the sky is bright blue with white clouds.
mechanism: A two-character chase scene, with the hunter in the open and the victim behind rock, makes the stakes legible: one has a rifle and the other has sweat and a hiding spot.
composition: The red headline sits top right above the pursuer's head, the hiding figure occupies the left third at large scale and the armed figure the right third at smaller scale, with the boulder diagonal between them. The red arrow starts at the headline and points down-left to the victim, directing the eye along a Z from text to hider to hunter.
typography: Three words in thick red capitals with a black outline fill the top right and are the largest text in the frame. 'HIDE OR DIE' reads fully at 160x90, and it adds a survival ultimatum while the money from the title is not shown.
colors: Saturated cyan sky and green grass behind a red headline, a red jacket and a red arrow, so red appears three times as the shared accent. The grey boulder and the white faces separate from the green and blue, and the red text and arrow read as alarm.
psychology: Clenched teeth, wide eyes and sweat drops on the hider read as strain and fear, while the pursuer's bulging eyes, drool and rifle read as menace. The red headline and arrow reinforce danger; the signals are cartoon exaggeration.
partnership: The title says you are hunted for a million dollars; the thumbnail shows the hunt and a death ultimatum but nothing about the prize. The missing bounty leaves a question the title alone answers.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red HIDE OR DIE text first, then the sweating face behind the boulder along the arrow, then the toothy gunman at right.
art: Flat cartoon with thick outlines, simple shading on the rock and bushes, and a rifle drawn in more detailed black than the stick-bodied figures. Layers are consistent, the background is clean and bold, and the headline, red jacket and gunman all survive at phone size.
strength: Two characters with opposite expressions and a rifle show the premise in one glance.
weakness: The $1 Million in the title has no visual counterpart, so the stakes read as generic danger rather than a bounty.
bottleneck: Without a money object, the thumbnail tells a chase story that any survival title could use.
action: Hypothesis: add a small bounty poster or cash bundle near the gunman to test whether tying the chase to money improves the title-image match.
counterexample: Seq 17 shows a single tearful figure beside a thin handwritten line, where this frame stages two characters in a visible conflict.
expression_label: clenched teeth, sweat drops, wide eyes
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: LOCAL [banner wordmark on roof cloth: airbnb]
scene: A bright red 3D house with an open dark entry and white steps stands in a street of white clay-style buildings, with a white banner reading airbnb draped over the front of the roof and a Greek flag on a pole at the top right. Two blue faceless figures crouch on the roof edge above the banner. At the lower left a small red figure kneels on the pavement with both hands on its head, under a black speech-pointer label reading LOCAL.
mechanism: Colour-coded figures stage a takeover: blue figures sit on top of the house while the red kneeling figure outside is tagged LOCAL, and the Greek flag fixes the place.
composition: The red house sits dead centre as the largest mass with steps leading to the bottom edge, while the black LOCAL label and the small red kneeling figure sit lower left as the secondary focus. The two blue figures and flag on top form a second cluster at the upper right, and the grey streets around them are mostly empty.
typography: One real word, LOCAL, in white bold capitals on a black speech label, plus the airbnb wordmark on the banner in red lowercase. At 160x90 both read, although LOCAL is small, and neither the title's 10 Years nor Athens appears in text.
colors: Pure white and light grey desaturated city against a single saturated red house, with two small blue figures as the only other hue and a blue-and-white flag at upper right. The red is the dominant mass and the isolated figures read as opposing sides.
psychology: The kneeling figure with hands on its head is a visible distress pose, and the blue figures crouched on the roof read as occupying the space. Faceless 3D figures carry no facial expression, so the emotion comes from posture and colour alone.
partnership: The title asks what Airbnb did to Athens over 10 years; the thumbnail answers with a branded house taken over from above and a displaced local. The 10-year span and city name are carried only by the flag and the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the large red house first, then the airbnb banner, then the LOCAL label and the kneeling red figure at lower left, and the blue figures on the roof last.
art: Clean 3D render with soft shadows, clay-white buildings and a single glossy red object, with the banner cloth showing believable folds. The kneeling figure is only about as tall as the bottom steps, so it is the smallest legible element at phone size.
strength: One saturated red house on a pale street gives a bold focal shape that carries the brand, the place and the power imbalance.
weakness: The kneeling LOCAL figure that holds the human side of the story is small and low on the frame.
bottleneck: At 160x90 the red house reads, but the tiny kneeling figure and the small LOCAL tag are the pieces that say who is affected.
action: Hypothesis: scale the LOCAL label and kneeling figure up by about 50 percent to test whether the displaced-local side reads at phone size.
counterexample: Seq 13 puts the viewer-addressed word YOU on a face-led scene, where this frame has only faceless figures.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A vertical split shows an orange cartoon figure lying back on a dark navy couch at the left, with a faceless oval head holding two white eye holes and a small dumbbell icon on the forehead, a softly rounded belly and teal shorts. The right panel on a blue ground shows an orange torso cropped at the neck with visible abdominal muscles and teal shorts with white drawcords. A thin black line divides the panels, and the left background is white.
mechanism: A relaxed couch pose beside a muscled torso turns the title's laziness-versus-results promise into a before-and-after picture with no words.
composition: The frame is split roughly in half by a vertical line, with the reclining figure running diagonally across the left and the upright torso filling the right edge to edge. The torso is cropped at the neck and thighs, so the abs sit at the centre of the right panel and the couch figure's head sits at the upper left.
typography: No words appear anywhere on the image. The title therefore carries all verbal information, and the thumbnail adds only the pose contrast and the dumbbell icon on the forehead.
colors: One orange skin tone and teal shorts are repeated across both panels, against a white-and-navy left and a flat blue right. The shared orange and teal bind the two panels as one subject, and the high saturation holds at phone size.
psychology: The left figure's wide round eyes and slack pose read as resting or passive, and the right torso reads as lean and defined. The contrast implies a transformation, but no face is visible on the right and no emotion is drawn.
partnership: The title says this is the laziest way to lose belly fat and that it works; the thumbnail shows a reclining body and a defined torso but no method. The how stays unanswered, and the picture implies a result without showing a cause.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the bright orange abs on the right first, then the reclining figure's softer belly at left, then the two white eye holes on the head.
art: Flat-shaded cartoon with dark orange outlines and simple highlight shapes on the muscles. The two panels share a character, but the belly on the left is only mildly rounded, so the contrast with the right is gentle, and both bodies read clearly at 160x90.
strength: The orange-and-teal split makes a before-and-after contrast clear without any text.
weakness: The left body is only mildly soft and the right torso has no head, so the change is not tied to one identifiable subject.
bottleneck: With no text and no method object, the image states the result but gives no clue to what the lazy way is.
action: Hypothesis: add one prop to the couch panel, such as a remote or a drink, to test whether naming the lazy behaviour increases the title-image link.
counterexample: Seq 8 loads three body panels, arrows and a headline onto its image, where this frame relies on a single split and no words.
expression_label: blank oval face with round eyes
medical_notes: The effortless-looking pose beside defined abs implies an easy body change; whether the video supports an effortless result is unchecked.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: 7 MOST / HARMFUL / FOODS FOR / YOUR COLON [item labels: Almond Milk, LOW-FAT, ARTIFICIAL SWEETENER, PROTEIN BAR, PROTEIN]
scene: A large pink-beige colon model with dark red lesion marks along its folds occupies the right side, and seven foods are each ringed in yellow circles around it: almond milk with crackers, a low-fat berry yogurt, a bowl of spinach, a bowl of sugar cubes, a bowl of artificial sweetener sachets, a protein bar, and a protein shaker with powder. The headline column runs down the left over a blurred blue clinical background.
mechanism: Seven circled foods ringing an ulcerated-looking colon turn a harm claim into an inventory the viewer wants to check against their own kitchen.
composition: The colon is the largest mass at the right-centre, the four-line headline occupies the left third, and the seven yellow-ringed foods orbit the colon at the edges. The headline and organ balance, but the ring of items on three sides makes the right half busy.
typography: Four lines: 7 MOST in yellow, HARMFUL in yellow, FOODS FOR in white and YOUR COLON in white on a red bar, all in heavy outlined capitals. The first two lines read at 160x90; the circled item labels do not. The words swap the title's 'secretly' and 'healthy' framing for a plain harm claim.
colors: Blue-grey blurred background with yellow and white headline words, a red bar behind YOUR COLON, and pink-red lesions on the colon. The yellow rings tie the foods together, and the red bar and lesions read as danger cues against the cool blue.
psychology: No person appears; the fear cue is the dark red lesions on the colon and the red label bar. Spinach and almond milk are ringed in the same yellow as the sugar and sweetener, which flattens healthy and unhealthy foods into one threat.
partnership: The title says 7 supposedly healthy foods secretly damage your gut; the thumbnail shows seven foods and a damaged colon, but drops the healthy-looking twist. It names items visually rather than answering which are worst, so the list stays open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow 7 MOST HARMFUL text first, then the lesioned colon, then the red YOUR COLON bar, then the ringed foods one by one.
art: Photoreal-looking food and organ renders composited over a blurred hospital-style background with consistent yellow outlines. The colon's surface and lesion marks are detailed, but the foods are small, and at 160x90 only the headline and the colon silhouette hold.
strength: A numbered headline and a visibly marked colon state the topic and the stakes together.
weakness: Spinach and a low-fat yogurt ringed in the same yellow as the sugar make the harm claim look indiscriminate.
bottleneck: The seven food icons are small and cluttered around the organ, so the specific foods are invisible at 160x90.
action: Hypothesis: show only three oversized foods around the colon to test whether fewer, larger items read better than seven small ones.
counterexample: Seq 15 pairs a single cup and one arrow with one colon, where this frame rings seven foods around the organ.
medical_notes: Packaging pairs spinach, almond milk and yogurt with a lesioned colon image, which implies visible damage from those foods without any stated evidence on the image.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: SO YOU WANT TO / OWN A CAFE [storefront sign BREW & BLOOM CAFE; chalkboard GOOD COFFEE GREAT FOOD GOOD VIBES; menu board COFFEE PASTRIES FOOD FREE WIFI; six captions: Market Research & Location Analysis, Marketing, Branding & Customer Loyalty, Startup Costs & Equipment Investment, Operating Costs & Staff Management, Menu Pricing & Profit Margins, Profitability & Business Growth]
scene: A watercolour-and-ink style storefront labelled BREW & BLOOM CAFE with a striped black-and-white awning, an open glass front, a chalkboard sign and a menu board stands in the middle, framed by trees and potted plants. Around it sit a green rising chart over stacked banknotes and coins at left, a clipboard, a target with stars at right, a gold coin stack with a dollar sign at the lower right, and six underlined captions linked by thin curved arrows.
mechanism: A neat illustrated storefront ringed by cost and revenue captions frames cafe ownership as a checklist of business topics rather than a single hook.
composition: The huge two-line headline across the top is the first anchor, and a red underline separates it from the cafe at the centre, with captions and icons arranged around the shop in a loose ring. Thin curved arrows from the captions point toward the building, which gives symmetry but leaves the eye with many small stops.
typography: Seven headline words in very heavy black capitals over two lines dominate the frame, with a red hand-drawn underline. Below them are six small captions and three short sign texts, all too small to read at 160x90, so only the headline carries.
colors: White background with black headline, a warm tan storefront and green trees, plus green banknotes, gold coins and a thin red underline as the money accents. Contrast is high for the headline and low for the small captions, and no colour signals alarm.
psychology: No person or face appears. The cues are money icons, a rising chart and a welcoming storefront, which read as an optimistic business invitation rather than a warning.
partnership: The title is The Economics of Owning a Cafe; the thumbnail restates the idea as a so-you-want-to invitation and previews the cost topics as captions. It adds the framing and a named shop but no surprising number or twist.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the black SO YOU WANT TO OWN A CAFE headline first, then the storefront and its sign, then the money icons at left and lower right, with the small captions last.
art: Detailed ink-and-wash illustration with coherent perspective and soft shading, set inside a dense ring of tiny captions and icons. The headline and shop survive at 160x90 as black text and a brown box, but the captions blur into grey marks.
strength: A seven-word heavy headline over a recognisable cafe makes the topic unmistakable.
weakness: Six captions, three signs and three icon groups surround the shop at a size that cannot be read on a phone.
bottleneck: The detail around the cafe is invisible at 160x90, so the image delivers only a generic cafe and a headline.
action: Hypothesis: remove the six captions and keep only the chart and coin stack to test whether a simpler cost-versus-income image holds attention better.
counterexample: Seq 2 states one claim and one subject on a plain scene, where this frame spreads many items around its subject.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: WHAT YOUR / BELLY / MEANS! / 3 FATAL SHAPES
scene: At the right a man with grey hair and a grey beard, a white coat and stethoscope looks straight ahead with a closed mouth against a red background. Below him three illustrated belly panels sit side by side: a round protruding belly, a belly sagging over a teal waistband, and a belly with visible folds. Two red arrows point at the panels, one from the word BELLY and one from the purple bar, and a hand points at the lower right panel.
mechanism: A doctor-styled stare, a giant BELLY word and three labelled belly drawings make the title's body-shape-as-diagnosis claim feel urgent through the word FATAL.
composition: The headline stack fills the left 55 percent in descending scale with BELLY largest, and the man's face sits upper right with the belly panel strip across the bottom right. Two red arrows overlap the text edge and the panels, so the lower area is crowded and the final S of SHAPES is partly covered by an arrowhead.
typography: Four lines of heavy capitals: WHAT yellow, YOUR white, BELLY in very large yellow, MEANS! white, then 3 FATAL SHAPES in white on a purple bar. BELLY and MEANS! read at 160x90, while the last letter of SHAPES is hidden by the arrowhead. The wording nearly copies the title's first clause and adds only the number.
colors: Black-purple left side with yellow and white lettering, a saturated red-orange panel behind the man, red arrows and a purple label bar. The red and the word FATAL read as danger, and the yellow BELLY gets the strongest contrast.
psychology: The man's level stare, closed mouth and white coat give an authoritative, serious cue, and the word FATAL with red arrows adds a fear cue. The belly drawings invite self-comparison.
partnership: The title asks what belly shape reveals about health with 3 Fatal Types; the thumbnail repeats the question and the number and adds three body drawings. It does not say which shape is worst, which keeps the question open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the giant yellow BELLY first, then the man's face, then the red arrows into the three belly panels, with the purple 3 FATAL SHAPES bar last.
art: Photo-style cutout of the man on a red gradient next to flat-illustrated belly panels, so a real face sits beside cartoon bodies. A partly cut-off embroidery on the coat is not readable, and the arrows and finger crowd the lower right.
strength: BELLY in giant yellow capitals is the clearest keyword, and the panels show what the title's shapes might look like.
weakness: Two red arrows and a pointing hand pile onto the lower right and clip the end of the SHAPES label.
bottleneck: The three panels are small relative to the headline, so the fatal shapes the title promises are hard to tell apart at 160x90.
action: Hypothesis: delete one red arrow and widen the purple bar so the last word is fully visible, to test whether a cleaner label improves the read.
counterexample: Seq 5 shows a calm before-and-after torso split with no text, where this frame stacks four lines of text and arrows.
medical_notes: The word FATAL plus a white-coat figure implies body shape diagnoses disease, and no credential is legible on the image.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon older man with swept grey hair, round glasses and a grey beard wears a navy blazer over a light blue patterned shirt and holds both hands out palms up in a shrug. A blue sweat drop sits on his forehead, his eyes glance to his right toward the text, and his mouth shows a crooked half-smile with visible teeth. The ground is plain white with no other objects.
mechanism: A shrugging, sweating cartoon man next to an either-or question visualises the title's dilemma without adding any new information beyond the pose.
composition: three-line headline fills the right half in centred, progressively indented lines
typography: Five heavy black words over three lines, with RETIRE RICH on a yellow highlight bar, OR RETIRE and EARLY? below in black on white. All lines read at 160x90, the highlight bar gives the first line priority, and the wording repeats the title's own phrase without the parenthetical tease.
colors: Pure white ground with black capitals, a single yellow bar as the loudest accent, and a navy blazer with a pale blue shirt on the figure. Contrast is maximal for the text and moderate for the figure, with no warning colours.
psychology: The sweat drop, uneven half-smile and shrugging open palms read as uncertainty or awkward indecision. The glance toward the headline directs attention to the question; no alarm cue appears.
partnership: The title says retire rich versus retire early and promises what they do not tell you; the thumbnail repeats the either-or and shows the choice as a shrug. The hidden-information promise in the title's parenthesis has no visual counterpart.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow RETIRE RICH bar first, then the sweating face and shrug, then OR RETIRE EARLY? beneath it.
art: Clean cartoon with thin dark outlines, light shading on the blazer and a flat white ground, so there is no compositing seam. The man's shrug and the headline stay legible at phone size.
strength: A yellow-highlighted first line and a shrugging figure make the either-or choice instantly readable.
weakness: The headline copies the title almost word for word, so the text adds no new fact.
bottleneck: Nothing in the image hints at what the two retirement paths contain, so the question stays abstract.
action: Hypothesis: replace EARLY? with a one-word cost difference on a second bar to test whether a concrete contrast outperforms the repeated question.
counterexample: Seq 20 places a leisurely figure beside a safe and cash, which shows the outcome that this frame only asks about.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: LOOK IN THE MIRROR / YOUR FACE / 4 HEART SIGNS AFTER 60
scene: At the right a balding man with short grey hair and a grey beard in a white coat over teal scrubs, with a stethoscope around his neck, points at his chin with one hand and holds a round hand mirror with the other against a flat red background. At the lower left an inset photo of an older person's ear shows a diagonal crease across the earlobe, ringed in a red circle with a red arrow pointing at it. The text column sits on a black left side.
mechanism: Telling the viewer to grab a mirror and pointing at his own face, with an ear crease circled, turns a symptom claim into a self-check the viewer can do immediately.
composition: The doctor-styled figure fills the right 40 percent with face and mirror at similar height, while the three text lines and the ear inset stack down the left. The red circle and arrow give the inset a focal point, and the pointing finger leads the eye from the face back toward the text.
typography: Three tiers: LOOK IN THE MIRROR in white, a very large yellow YOUR FACE, and 4 HEART SIGNS AFTER 60 on a red bar with HEART in yellow. YOUR FACE and the first line read at 160x90, while the bar line becomes small. The text repeats the title's face, heart and 60 terms and adds the mirror instruction.
colors: Black left panel with yellow and white capitals, a saturated red panel behind the figure, and a red bar and red circle as the repeated accent. The yellow and red read as warning, and teal scrubs and a white coat give the figure a clean medical coding.
psychology: Raised brows, a slightly open mouth and a finger pointing at his chin create a direct instructing look. The white coat, stethoscope and red bar signal medical authority and alarm, though no credential is legible.
partnership: The title lists four heart warning signs on the face after 60 and says to grab a mirror; the thumbnail repeats the mirror, the 4 and the 60, and adds one concrete example, a creased earlobe. Which three other signs exist stays unanswered.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow YOUR FACE first, then the man's face and mirror, then the red 4 HEART SIGNS bar, then the circled earlobe inset last.
art: Photo-style cutout of the man with consistent lighting against a flat red field, and a photographic close-up inset with a drawn red circle and arrow. The text, figure and inset are well separated, but the ear crease inset is small and low in contrast.
strength: A direct mirror instruction, a pointing gesture and a circled ear crease turn the claim into an action.
weakness: Three text lines, a bar, a figure, a mirror and an inset compete for attention in one frame.
bottleneck: The circled earlobe, which is the only visible sign, is small and low in contrast at 160x90.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the circled-ear inset to double its size and drop the first white line to test whether the single sign carries the claim.
counterexample: Seq 17 has one drawn figure and a short handwritten line, where this frame stacks three lines, a bar and an inset.
hero_object: hand mirror and circled earlobe crease
medical_notes: A circled earlobe crease presented as a heart sign and a white-coat figure with no legible credential could read as a self-diagnosis claim without supporting evidence on the image.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon figure with a white face, shaggy brown hair, wide eyes glancing down to its right and an open smiling mouth wears a fur tunic and holds up a brown chocolate-like chunk in one hand. At the right a flat stone table holds a split cocoa pod with dark beans spilling out and a few loose beans. Behind the figure is a hut or cave opening showing a blue sky and green field, framed by brown walls.
mechanism: A delighted caveman holding a brown chunk beside a split cocoa pod answers 'when did ancient humans discover chocolate' with a first-taste moment.
composition: The headline runs across the whole top, the figure sits at the left with a large head, and the stone table with the pod is a diagonal counterweight at the right. The blue sky in the opening is the single cool shape in the middle, which frames the space between figure and table.
typography: Two words, COCOA FIRST?, in yellow outlined capitals with thinner strokes than a heavy headline, spanning the full width. Both words are readable at 160x90, though the outline is lighter than the other headlines in this batch, and the text does not repeat the title's wording.
colors: Warm brown and tan scene with a yellow headline, a pale blue sky and olive green field for the only cool accents, and dark brown cocoa matching the figure's hair. The brown-on-brown figure and pod sit low in contrast, but the white face separates cleanly.

scene: A cartoon man with short orange hair, a heavy chin, a grey T-shirt, wide round eyes looking down to his right and an open mouth stands at the left. At the right a tall stack of green dollar bills and a shorter, flatter stack sit on a thin grey ground line, with a few scattered coins in front. A black curved arrow starts above the tall stack and points down at the shorter stack.
mechanism: A shocked cartoon man beside a tall stack that an arrow shrinks to a short one makes the paradox in the title, more income but less wealth, visible.
composition: The man fills the left third at large scale, the two-line headline sits at the top right, and the two cash stacks run along the lower right with the arrow between them. The arrow carries the eye from the tall stack to the short one, and the white space between headline and stacks keeps the frame uncluttered.
typography: Three words in very heavy black condensed capitals over two lines, with an ellipsis after MORE MONEY and a ?! after POORER. Both lines read at 160x90, and the wording puts the paradox without repeating the title's two incomes.
colors: White ground with black type, green banknotes as the only saturated colour, and a grey T-shirt and orange hair on the figure. The green stacks stand out against the white and grey, and no red or warning colour appears.
psychology: Wide round eyes and an open mouth give a visible shock or disbelief expression. The shrinking stack and the arrow reinforce a loss cue.
partnership: The title says two incomes made the middle class poorer; the thumbnail drops the two-incomes cause and shows the paradox as a shrinking stack. The cause remains unanswered, which keeps the how-did-that-happen question open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the black MORE MONEY... POORER?! headline first, then the shocked face, then the tall stack and the arrow to the short stack.
art: Flat cartoon with thick outlines and clear shapes: a large head, a simple T-shirt and detailed dollar bills with curling edges. Everything sits on a white ground with no compositing seams, so face, headline and stacks all read at phone size.
strength: A shocked face, a tall stack, an arrow and a short stack explain the paradox without any other element.
weakness: The generic cartoon man has no house, paycheque or family object to tie him to the middle-class subject.
bottleneck: The two incomes in the title have no picture, so the cause of the shrinking stack is invisible.
action: Hypothesis: place two small paycheque icons above the tall stack to test whether the two-incomes cause becomes legible.
